title: Budget, Readout or Reasoning? Where Small Reasoning Models Lose Value in Auction Bidding
abstract: arXiv:2611.34068v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Ad platforms and marketplaces show bidders a bid landscape, the estimated chance of winning at each candidate bid, and increasingly let agents built on reasoning language models choose the bid. We give six open reasoning models of 4B to 14B parameters such landscapes, with win curves from eBay closing prices and from a simulated advertising market (AuctionNet), and score their bids on held-out auctions against an exact calculator. Because the agent is handed the estimates, the lost value can be split by cause. Two failures belong to the models. They pass over the best option even when the values written in their own trace already rank it first, and their wrong answers lean toward the highest bid on the menu. The lean is about the bid's size, not its place in the list, and it survives sampling. At 768 forced tokens on eBay, under pay-your-bid pricing, the wrong answers cost bidders 7-17% of the surplus the calculator's bids earn. Arithmet

translated_title: 预算、读取还是推理？小型推理模型在拍卖竞价中于何处损失价值
translated_abstract: 广告平台和市场会向竞标者展示“出价景观”，即在每个候选出价下获胜的估计概率，并且越来越多地让基于推理语言模型构建的智能体来选择出价。我们向六个参数量为4B至14B的开源推理模型提供了这样的出价景观，其获胜曲线来自eBay的成交价格和一个模拟的广告市场（AuctionNet），并在留出的拍卖上对照一个精确计算器对它们的出价进行评分。由于获胜概率估计是直接交给智能体的，因此损失的价值可以按原因进行拆分。两类失败归属于模型自身：即使其推理轨迹中写下的数值已经把最优选项排在第一位，它们仍会跳过该选项；而且它们的错误答案倾向于选择菜单中出价最高的选项。这种倾向与出价的大小有关，而非其在列表中的位置，并且在采样中依然存在。在eBay数据上、在“按出价付费”的定价机制下、强制生成768个token时，错误答案使竞标者损失了计算器出价所能获得盈余的7-17%。算术……
tldr: 该论文将六个4B至14B参数的开源推理模型置于基于真实eBay成交价和模拟广告市场的拍卖出价景观中，并对照精确计算器按原因拆分其价值损失，首次揭示损失主要源于模型自身的两类推理失败——忽视自身轨迹中已排名第一的最优选项、错误答案系统性偏向最高出价——导致竞标者损失7-17%的盈余。
en_tdlr: The paper scores six 4B-14B open reasoning models' bids against an exact calculator using real eBay win curves and a simulated ad market, attributing the lost value to two model-inherent failures—overlooking the best option already ranked first in their own traces and a size-driven bias toward the highest bid—which cost bidders 7-17% of the surplus.
